messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: high token queue depth detected on model-gpu-3 (us-west-2). Alert I-2026-0112 triggered at 2026-03-14T22:05:22Z. Severity: P1. Paging oncall@redwood.
ryan: oncall here, looking. grabbing the runbook now.
maya: fyi — noticed tail latency spike in prod traces, customer 0.2% error rate but large latency outliers. tagging @ryan.
sam: are we seeing any failed model loads or OOMs? logs from runtime look ok.
ryan: no OOMs. queues are backing up on gpu-3 pool. suspect KV cache thrash after recent rollout. checking cache hit metrics.
liz: i pushed the new kernel last night — could be regression. checking rollout status for gpu-3 nodes.
eva: copying relevant grafana link: https://grafana/redwood/d/model-serving/queue-depth?orgId=1&var-pool=gpu-3
ryan: provisional mitigation: increment pool size by +2 and temporarily enable aggressive batching disable to reduce queue depth. will run scale up and watch.
observability-bot: action logged: scaling request sent to infra-orchestrator (change_id: ch-9421).
ryan: scaling started. also creating a silence for non-page alerts to reduce noise while we stabilize.
maya: +1 on silence for low-priority warnings — we want only true pages now.
sam: if scaling doesn't help, plan B is to rollback kernel or pin older model variant.
ryan: scale completed at 22:12Z. queue depth trending down but still above thresholds for a minute. watching for 5m.
observability-bot: Alert I-2026-0112 status: pending -> resolved at 22:18:03Z (auto).
ryan: confirmed queues back to normal. latency p95 dropped back under SLO. marking as mitigated.
maya: quick customer impact note: product analytics shows small fraction of requests delayed; support ticket count unchanged. will mark customer impact as minimal.
liz: rolling kernel update paused for gpu-3 pools. will hold until post-incident review.
eva: created a dashboard snapshot and added a panel for "queue depth by model shard" — sharing link in the runbook.
ryan: post-incident actions we should take in next 24h: 1) tune alert thresholds to reduce noisy pages 2) add an automated knob to scale on queue depth 3) validate KV cache behavior for the new kernel.
maya: on thresholds — current rule fires on 3m > 400. i propose raising to 600 with 5m window and add a secondary warning alert that doesn't page.
ryan: agree. also add a short 'for' 5m to avoid momentary spikes. sample proposed alert rule below:
```yaml
- alert: ModelTokenQueueDepthHigh
  expr: sum_over_time(redwood_model_queue_depth{pool="gpu-3"}[5m]) > 600
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
```
sam: let's also add a non-paging alert for 400-600 with severity: ticket so we can track without paging.
liz: i'll open a tiny PR to update alertmanager config and add a doc note.
eva: i'm going to schedule a maintenance window for the kernel rollout so it won't interrupt during business hours. proposed: 2026-03-15 02:00-04:00 UTC.
ryan: sounds good. also we need to clean up silences after we finish validating thresholds. set silence TTL to 6h and ensure owners listed.
maya: test plan: apply threshold change in staging, run load test to simulate KV cache thrash, validate queue depth and latency. if stable, roll to prod with canary.
ryan: assigning: liz -> update alert rules PR, eva -> dashboard + maintenance window, sam -> run cache load tests, maya -> coordinate canary and validation. I'll follow up in #eng-oncall with status.
observability-bot: silence created for alert template ModelTokenQueueDepthWarning (silence_id: s-779) duration 6h, creators: ryan.
liz: PR opened: fixes/alerts/raise-queue-thresholds (link). please review.
sam: started load test in staging. initial results: queue depth stays below 450 with proposed kernel disabled. pushing more load now.
maya: small note — add a datapoint to the dashboard for "alert flapping rate" so we can detect noisy thresholds over time.
eva: maintenance window scheduled and annotated in runbook.
ryan: will validate new thresholds for 48h post-deploy and then remove temporary silence. leaving action items in the incident notes.
incident-bot: INCIDENT I-2026-0112 marked RESOLVED at 2026-03-14T22:46:05Z. Tags: mitigation:scale, followup:alert-tuning.
ryan: thanks all. we'll reconvene tomorrow for the postmortem and to decide whether to revert the kernel or continue with additional cache hardening.
maya: added reminder to postmortem: include customer impact timeline and alert noise graph.
liz: once PR is approved i'll coordinate with release to schedule canary during maintenance window.
eva: i'll remove silence after 48h validation or earlier if we see no regressions.
sam: uploading load-test artifacts to the incident thread.
ryan: closing thread for now. if anyone discovers resurgence, ping oncall and reopen. :thumbsup:
